changesets.summary: Keep creator handovers compatible with graduation
changesets.details:
##### User impact

The new creator must accept a handover by signing it. A creator or partner cannot occupy the base mint's graduation account slot, preventing these account aliases from trapping a completed launch's reserves.

review_request.title: fix(curve)!: require accepted creator handovers and valid LP recipients
fix(curve)!: require accepted creator handovers and valid LP recipients

changesets.summary: Require accepted creator handovers
changesets.details: `SetLaunchCreator` adds a required `new_creator_signer` account matching the requested creator. Both creators sign, preventing handovers to deterministic graduation accounts that cannot accept them. Reject the base mint as a successor and reject launch creation when a nonzero LP recipient aliases that mint. The CLI adds `--new-creator-keypair`.

review_request.title: fix(curve)!: require accepted creator handovers and valid LP recipients
fix(curve)!: require accepted creator handovers and valid LP recipients

changesets.summary: Give every launch its own graduation pool
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Two launches cannot claim the same future market by swapping their base and quote tokens. New launches use the larger mint address as the base token; the CLI chooses a compatible address automatically. Existing mints must follow that ordering.

review_request.title: fix(curve)!: reserve unique graduation pools with canonical mint roles
fix(curve)!: reserve unique graduation pools with canonical mint roles

changesets.summary: Assign canonical mint roles before trading
changesets.details: Launch creation requires the base mint to sort after the quote mint by address bytes. Since a base mint has one launch PDA, each accepted launch now uniquely identifies the AMM's unordered pair and tier; reciprocal launches fail before minting supply or accepting trades. The CLI generates compatible mint keys automatically and checks existing mint addresses. Graduation uses the established quote-as-token-0 invariant directly, removing its two-way mint-role selection.

review_request.title: fix(curve)!: reserve unique graduation pools with canonical mint roles
fix(curve)!: reserve unique graduation pools with canonical mint roles

changesets.summary: Client journeys and a performance gate
changesets.details:
- Every instruction now has one ordered journey on a live Surfnet through the generated Rust client (`every_instruction_runs_in_one_journey`) and through the generated TypeScript client (`typescript_client_runs_every_instruction`), which the Rust side drives with funded fixtures — the restricted AMM tier, both mints, and every derived address — and then checks the resulting on-chain state, so the TypeScript client's wire format is proven end to end against the deployed program beside the pinned AMM. The TypeScript journey asserts its PDA helpers reproduce the Rust-derived addresses before sending anything.
- The journeys' keypairs are seeded, so identical binaries measure identical compute units.
- A `performance` workflow benchmarks the pull request against its base (each side against its own `amm.rev`): deployed binary size plus every instruction's compute units (median of three journey runs), posted as one consolidated PR comment. The policy fails the check on any binary-size increase or a compute-unit regression above 2%, unless the pull request carries `performance-approved`. `scripts/benchmark.ts` and `scripts/compare-benchmarks.ts` run the same pipeline locally.
- `docs/performance.md` documents the pipeline and the policy.

review_request.title: test(pina_bonding_curve): drive every instruction through each client and gate performance
test(pina_bonding_curve): drive every instruction through each client and gate performance

changesets.summary: Complete launches at the promised funding amount
changesets.details:
##### User impact

A launch cannot complete below its configured funding threshold. Curve designs whose price precision cannot represent that amount are refused when the configuration is created.

review_request.title: fix(curve)!: reject inexact migration thresholds
fix(curve)!: reject inexact migration thresholds

changesets.summary: Reject unrepresentable migration thresholds
changesets.details:
Configuration creation rejects a migration threshold when flooring its derived price would raise less quote than requested. Curve designs previously accepted with an inexact threshold must choose an exactly representable amount. Every accepted threshold equals the quote used to derive migration supply and complete a full buy.

Track the actual quote still required through each segment instead of maintaining a second accumulated total. A partial segment must consume the exact remaining amount before the configuration is accepted.

review_request.title: fix(curve)!: reject inexact migration thresholds
fix(curve)!: reject inexact migration thresholds

changesets.summary: Choose the least you will accept for a trade
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Buying and selling now require an exact minimum output. Choose it using a price source you trust; even a dishonest RPC cannot lower that limit when the CLI signs your trade.

review_request.title: fix(cli)!: require explicit minimum trade outputs
fix(cli)!: require explicit minimum trade outputs

changesets.summary: Require explicit trade output limits
changesets.details: CLI buys require `--minimum-base-out` and sales require `--minimum-quote-out`, both nonzero. Remove `--slippage-bps`: simulation events from the selected RPC are advisory and never determine the signed floor. Display the exact minimum before signing and in the result.

review_request.title: fix(cli)!: require explicit minimum trade outputs
fix(cli)!: require explicit minimum trade outputs

changesets.summary: Graduation works for launchpads that launch their own tokens
changesets.details:
##### User impact

A partner who launches a token under their own launchpad can now graduate it to the open market: both LP payouts are merged into one payment to their wallet. Handing a launch to the unset default address is refused instead of locking that launch's creator earnings forever.

review_request.title: fix(pina_bonding_curve): merge same-owner LP payouts and refuse default creators
fix(pina_bonding_curve): merge same-owner LP payouts and refuse default creators

changesets.summary: Harden graduation payouts and creator handover
changesets.details:
- A partner who launches under their own configuration no longer bricks graduation: when the launch creator and the partner are the same address, the creator and partner LP shares are paid as one transfer to that address's LP token account instead of naming the same writable account twice, which the runtime rejects.
- `SetLaunchCreator` rejects the default address, which could otherwise hold creator rights that can never sign, leaving fees and the vested allocation unclaimable forever.
- `Graduate` asserts the launch's price equals the configuration's migration price before seeding the pool, turning any future state drift into a failed transaction instead of a mispriced pool.

review_request.title: fix(pina_bonding_curve): merge same-owner LP payouts and refuse default creators
fix(pina_bonding_curve): merge same-owner LP payouts and refuse default creators

changesets.summary: Mis-sent quote is no longer stranded
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Quote tokens sent straight to a launch's vault used to sit above the launch's accounting forever. Anyone can now call `SweepQuoteDust` to split that stray balance between the token's creator and the launchpad by the configured fee share, before or after graduation, and creator handovers are visible in transaction logs.

review_request.title: feat(pina_bonding_curve): emit creator-handover events and sweep quote dust
feat(pina_bonding_curve): emit creator-handover events and sweep quote dust

changesets.summary: Creator-handover events and a dust sweep
changesets.details:
- `SetLaunchCreator` emits `LaunchCreatorChanged` with the previous and new creator, so indexers follow creator-rights changes without polling accounts.
- A new permissionless `SweepQuoteDust` instruction splits quote that arrived in a launch's quote vault above its accounting — a donation or a mis-sent transfer — into the creator's and partner's fee balances by the configuration's `creator_fee_share`. The reserve and accrued fees are never touched, and it works in every launch status. Emits `DustSwept`.
- Clients, IDL, and ABI layout regenerated for the new instruction and events.

review_request.title: feat(pina_bonding_curve): emit creator-handover events and sweep quote dust
feat(pina_bonding_curve): emit creator-handover events and sweep quote dust

changesets.summary: The bonding curve has its permanent address
changesets.details:
##### User impact

The bonding curve now lives at the address it will keep on mainnet, and launches graduate into the Pina AMM at its permanent address. Anything that saved the earlier test addresses needs to switch to the new ones. Security researchers can also find the project's private reporting channel directly from the deployed program.

review_request.title: chore(pina_bonding_curve)!: deploy under the mainnet identity Curve1Gqpq…BvP
chore(pina_bonding_curve)!: deploy under the mainnet identity Curve1Gqpq…BvP

changesets.summary: Move the program to its mainnet identity and graduate into the mainnet AMM
changesets.details:
The program id is now `Curve1GqpqznjxpJzH313L9CRhAehHaikb4SJMFQeBvP`, so every PDA moves with it: the AMM authority that graduation tiers must restrict pool creation to is now `HUjATWLMQR85P71zHVoHgbRPTY7xx4gEdyDg7EMin7XX`. `pina migrations create` rebound the unpublished migration history to the new id; `publications.json` still has no receipts.

Graduation now calls the Pina AMM at `pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi`. `amm.rev` pins the AMM commit that carries that identity, and `vendor/pina_amm` is re-imported from its IDL. The CPI, Rust, TypeScript, and Dart clients are regenerated with both ids, and `addresses.rs`, the docs, the website, and the tests name the new addresses.

The deployed binary now embeds a `security.txt` through `solana-security-txt` 1.1.3, only under `bpf-entrypoint`. It names the project, the private advisory form as contact, `SECURITY.md` as policy, and the source repository.

review_request.title: chore(pina_bonding_curve)!: deploy under the mainnet identity Curve1Gqpq…BvP
chore(pina_bonding_curve)!: deploy under the mainnet identity Curve1Gqpq…BvP

changesets.summary: A launch can no longer be handed to itself
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Handing a launch's creator rights to the launch's own address is refused. Before this change, a creator could do that to make a completed launch impossible to move to the open market, which left buyers' funds stuck in it.

review_request.title: fix(pina_bonding_curve): reject the launch itself as its creator
fix(pina_bonding_curve): reject the launch itself as its creator

changesets.summary: Reject the launch itself as its creator
changesets.details: `SetLaunchCreator` now fails with the new append-only error `LaunchAsCreator` (24) when `new_creator` is the launch's own address. The launch PDA can never sign, so its creator fees and vested allocation would be unclaimable, and with a nonzero `creator_lp_share` its LP payout targets the launch's own LP token account. `Graduate` then names that writable account twice, which Pina rejects as `DuplicateMutableAccount`, so no account list could graduate the launch and every trader's quote would stay locked in a completed launch. The Surfpool suite covers the rejection, and `docs/instructions.md` now lists error codes 22 to 24.

review_request.title: fix(pina_bonding_curve): reject the launch itself as its creator
fix(pina_bonding_curve): reject the launch itself as its creator

changesets.summary: Cheaper trades on a smaller program
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Every buy and sell now costs about 830 and 760 fewer compute units, and the deployed program is about 11 KB (9%) smaller, which lowers its rent. Trades no longer revalidate the price curve stored in an immutable configuration, copy only the pricing fields they need out of it, and share one compiled copy of the slow wide-division and signer-seed routines instead of a copy per call site. Nothing about the math, fees, or account layout changed.

review_request.title: perf(pina_bonding_curve): stop repricing configuration work on every trade
perf(pina_bonding_curve): stop repricing configuration work on every trade

changesets.summary: Trim the deployed program and trade compute
changesets.details: Stops repricing configuration work on every trade: stored curves are trusted instead of revalidated, the 256-bit division is compiled once, trades copy only the pricing fields out of a configuration, and signer seeds are built through one shared helper. The deployed binary shrinks by about 11 KB and buys and sells get about 830 and 760 compute units cheaper. No account, instruction, event, or wire format changes.

review_request.title: perf(pina_bonding_curve): stop repricing configuration work on every trade
perf(pina_bonding_curve): stop repricing configuration work on every trade

changesets.summary: Preview trades without authorizing them
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Quotes and commands run with `--simulate` no longer authorize an on-chain transaction. An RPC receiving a preview cannot reuse it to spend your tokens.

review_request.title: fix(cli): keep simulations cryptographically unsigned
fix(cli): keep simulations cryptographically unsigned

changesets.summary: Keep RPC simulations unsigned
changesets.details: The CLI constructs simulation transactions with zero signatures and a placeholder blockhash. Only the send path fetches a recent blockhash and signs, preventing an RPC from broadcasting a quote or preview transaction.

review_request.title: fix(cli): keep simulations cryptographically unsigned
fix(cli): keep simulations cryptographically unsigned

changesets.summary: Patch audited dependencies and document compression reachability
changesets.details:
Upgrade the CLI and separate Surfpool test workspace's transitive `zstd-sys` dependency to 2.1.2. Record three API-specific advisory exceptions for the SDK's required zstd 0.13 / zstd-safe 7 versions, with the exact unaffected RPC decoder path and disabled seekable feature documented in the security guide. All other advisory checks remain enforced.

Update the website's Zod and Undici dependencies to patched releases. Miniflare's exact Undici pin receives a version-specific override on the same 7.x line; the other updates stay within their existing parent ranges. No JavaScript advisory is suppressed.

review_request.title: fix(deps): patch audited compression and website dependencies
fix(deps): patch audited compression and website dependencies

sections.title: Breaking changes
entries:
#### Require accepted creator handovers

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #30](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/30)

`SetLaunchCreator` adds a required `new_creator_signer` account matching the requested creator. Both creators sign, preventing handovers to deterministic graduation accounts that cannot accept them. Reject the base mint as a successor and reject launch creation when a nonzero LP recipient aliases that mint. The CLI adds `--new-creator-keypair`.

#### Assign canonical mint roles before trading

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #31](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/31)

Launch creation requires the base mint to sort after the quote mint by address bytes. Since a base mint has one launch PDA, each accepted launch now uniquely identifies the AMM's unordered pair and tier; reciprocal launches fail before minting supply or accepting trades. The CLI generates compatible mint keys automatically and checks existing mint addresses. Graduation uses the established quote-as-token-0 invariant directly, removing its two-way mint-role selection.

#### Reject unrepresentable migration thresholds

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #29](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/29)

Configuration creation rejects a migration threshold when flooring its derived price would raise less quote than requested. Curve designs previously accepted with an inexact threshold must choose an exactly representable amount. Every accepted threshold equals the quote used to derive migration supply and complete a full buy.

Track the actual quote still required through each segment instead of maintaining a second accumulated total. A partial segment must consume the exact remaining amount before the configuration is accepted.

#### Require explicit trade output limits

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #27](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/27)

CLI buys require `--minimum-base-out` and sales require `--minimum-quote-out`, both nonzero. Remove `--slippage-bps`: simulation events from the selected RPC are advisory and never determine the signed floor. Display the exact minimum before signing and in the result.

#### Harden graduation payouts and creator handover

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #9](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/9)

- A partner who launches under their own configuration no longer bricks graduation: when the launch creator and the partner are the same address, the creator and partner LP shares are paid as one transfer to that address's LP token account instead of naming the same writable account twice, which the runtime rejects.
- `SetLaunchCreator` rejects the default address, which could otherwise hold creator rights that can never sign, leaving fees and the vested allocation unclaimable forever.
- `Graduate` asserts the launch's price equals the configuration's migration price before seeding the pool, turning any future state drift into a failed transaction instead of a mispriced pool.

#### Creator-handover events and a dust sweep

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #10](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/10)

- `SetLaunchCreator` emits `LaunchCreatorChanged` with the previous and new creator, so indexers follow creator-rights changes without polling accounts.
- A new permissionless `SweepQuoteDust` instruction splits quote that arrived in a launch's quote vault above its accounting — a donation or a mis-sent transfer — into the creator's and partner's fee balances by the configuration's `creator_fee_share`. The reserve and accrued fees are never touched, and it works in every launch status. Emits `DustSwept`.
- Clients, IDL, and ABI layout regenerated for the new instruction and events.

#### Move the program to its mainnet identity and graduate into the mainnet AMM

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #18](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/18)

The program id is now `Curve1GqpqznjxpJzH313L9CRhAehHaikb4SJMFQeBvP`, so every PDA moves with it: the AMM authority that graduation tiers must restrict pool creation to is now `HUjATWLMQR85P71zHVoHgbRPTY7xx4gEdyDg7EMin7XX`. `pina migrations create` rebound the unpublished migration history to the new id; `publications.json` still has no receipts.

Graduation now calls the Pina AMM at `pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi`. `amm.rev` pins the AMM commit that carries that identity, and `vendor/pina_amm` is re-imported from its IDL. The CPI, Rust, TypeScript, and Dart clients are regenerated with both ids, and `addresses.rs`, the docs, the website, and the tests name the new addresses.

The deployed binary now embeds a `security.txt` through `solana-security-txt` 1.1.3, only under `bpf-entrypoint`. It names the project, the private advisory form as contact, `SECURITY.md` as policy, and the source repository.

#### Reject the launch itself as its creator

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #16](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/16)

`SetLaunchCreator` now fails with the new append-only error `LaunchAsCreator` (24) when `new_creator` is the launch's own address.   _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #15](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/15)
- **Keep RPC simulations unsigned.** The CLI constructs simulation transactions with zero signatures and a placeholder blockhash. Only the send path fetches a recent blockhash and signs, preventing an RPC from broadcasting a quote or preview transaction.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #25](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/25)
#### Patch audited dependencies and document compression reachability

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #28](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/28)

Upgrade the CLI and separate Surfpool test workspace's transitive `zstd-sys` dependency to 2.1.2. Record three API-specific advisory exceptions for the SDK's required zstd 0.13 / zstd-safe 7 versions, with the exact unaffected RPC decoder path and disabled seekable feature documented in the security guide. All other advisory checks remain enforced.

Update the website's Zod and Undici dependencies to patched releases. Miniflare's exact Undici pin receives a version-specific override on the same 7.x line; the other updates stay within their existing parent ranges. No JavaScript advisory is suppressed.

entries:
#### Keep creator handovers compatible with graduation

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #30](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/30)

##### User impact

The new creator must accept a handover by signing it. A creator or partner cannot occupy the base mint's graduation account slot, preventing these account aliases from trapping a completed launch's reserves.

#### Give every launch its own graduation pool

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #31](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/31)

##### User impact

Two launches cannot claim the same future market by swapping their base and quote tokens. New launches use the larger mint address as the base token; the CLI chooses a compatible address automatically. Existing mints must follow that ordering.

#### Complete launches at the promised funding amount

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #29](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/29)

##### User impact

A launch cannot complete below its configured funding threshold. Curve designs whose price precision cannot represent that amount are refused when the configuration is created.

#### Choose the least you will accept for a trade

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #27](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/27)

##### User impact

Buying and selling now require an exact minimum output. Choose it using a price source you trust; even a dishonest RPC cannot lower that limit when the CLI signs your trade.

#### Graduation works for launchpads that launch their own tokens

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #9](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/9)

##### User impact

A partner who launches a token under their own launchpad can now graduate it to the open market: both LP payouts are merged into one payment to their wallet. Handing a launch to the unset default address is refused instead of locking that launch's creator earnings forever.

#### Mis-sent quote is no longer stranded

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #10](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/10)

##### User impact

Quote tokens sent straight to a launch's vault used to sit above the launch's accounting forever. Anyone can now call `SweepQuoteDust` to split that stray balance between the token's creator and the launchpad by the configured fee share, before or after graduation, and creator handovers are visible in transaction logs.

#### The bonding curve has its permanent address

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #18](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/18)

##### User impact

The bonding curve now lives at the address it will keep on mainnet, and launches graduate into the Pina AMM at its permanent address. Anything that saved the earlier test addresses needs to switch to the new ones. Security researchers can also find the project's private reporting channel directly from the deployed program.

#### A launch can no longer be handed to itself

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #16](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/16)

##### User impact

Handing a launch's creator rights to the launch's own address is refused. Before this change, a creator could do that to make a completed launch impossible to move to the open market, which left buyers' funds stuck in it.

#### Cheaper trades on a smaller program

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #15](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/15)

##### User impact

Every buy and sell now costs about 830 and 760 fewer compute units, and the deployed program is about 11 KB (9%) smaller, which lowers its rent. Trades no longer revalidate the price curve stored in an immutable configuration, copy only the pricing fields they need out of it, and share one compiled copy of the slow wide-division and signer-seed routines instead of a copy per call site. Nothing about the math, fees, or account layout changed.

#### Preview trades without authorizing them

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #25](https://github.com/pina-rs/bonding_curve/pull/25)

##### User impact

Quotes and commands run with `--simulate` no longer authorize an on-chain transaction. An RPC receiving a preview cannot reuse it to spend your tokens.
